knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A check that names the surface, the condition and the way to see it can be confirmed by a second person. Vague wording such as 'looks clean' or added emphasis cannot.
An area with a known failure is not finished. Reopening the task, correcting the step and recording the failure and fix come before any sign-off.
Visitors see shared surfaces throughout the day, so an end-of-shift check alone can leave a marked state standing for hours.

practicalCriteria: Rewrites one vague control point from a supplied task sheet so that it names a surface, a condition and a way to see it, observed by the assessor.
Traces every step of a supplied three-step task to a control point, or identifies a step with no check, observed by the assessor.
Walks a supplied area, checks each control point in order, and records any failure with its fix, observed by the assessor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Rewritten control point on the supplied task sheet
Task sheet with the step-to-check links marked
Completed check record for the walk-through, including any failure and its fix
stopWorkCriteria: A control point cannot be checked because the area is unsafe, or the check needs a tool or PPE that has not been supplied
A failed check has been found and the area is about to be signed off without the fix being recorded
A person is asked to sign off an area that they have not inspected
